fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. Paul says, “I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries…” His contemporaries are the people his own age. So he was ahead of many of them, not falling behind. Paul didn't need a trophy for that.

Close, friend, but Paul shuts that door himself. He says, “I did not receive it from any man, nor was I taught it…” Teachers are people, so they're out. Paul says he received it “…by revelation from Jesus Christ.”

That's the opposite of what Paul says about his former way of life, friend. He says, “…how severely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.” Joining it and teaching its people isn't in his account. This is a heavy part, and I think Paul says it plainly.
Not quite, friend. Paul says he was “…extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.” Zealous means he cared a LOT and pushed hard. Unsure would be me standing at the oven asking if it's on.

Gentiles it is, baker. Paul says God was pleased to reveal His Son in him “…so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles…” Gentiles are people who aren't Jewish. And that's who Paul would preach to. Look at that, the man who persecuted the church is the one sent to preach Him.

Paul says no, friend. He writes, “…I did not rush to consult with flesh and blood…” Flesh and blood means people. He didn't go running to ask anybody about it. Me, I'd have been on the phone in seconds.

That's right, baker. Paul says, “…I did not rush to consult with flesh and blood…” Flesh and blood means people, so he didn't go running to ask anybody about it. Paul took another road, and we'll see which one next.
Syria and Cilicia, baker. Paul says, “Later I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.” Two regions, named right there in his own words. That's the answer straight from the letter.

Good guess, friend, since those are real places. Pontus and Bithynia show up in Peter's letter (1 Peter 1:1), but not in Paul's account here. Paul says, “Later I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.” Those are the two he names.

Paul says it the other way, friend. He writes, “I was personally unknown, however, to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.” So they didn't know him personally. Whatever they knew came from what they heard. The next verse tells us what that was.

Doubting isn't in the verse, friend. The churches hear, “The man who formerly persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.” The report says he's preaching it. That's the news that traveled.
